sources.title: MT-PingEval: Evaluating Multi-Turn Collaboration with Private Information Games
facts_used: Private-information collaborative games with automatic verification and generation of new instances
Fixed per-player communication-token budget evaluated across 2, 4, 8, and 16 turns; 128 tokens per player and 1000 generated examples per task in the reported experiment
Task families include chess, COVR, MD3, tangram, and structured-record name-game
Most tested models did not improve with more turns; some outcomes were attributable to guess-and-check behavior

sources.title: SILO-BENCH: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
facts_used: 30 algorithmic tasks spanning aggregation, mesh, and global-shuffle complexity levels
Six agent counts from 2 through 100 and three communication infrastructures yield 54 configurations
The paper defines token consumption as generated output tokens per communication round and also reports base-prompt, local-shard, and accumulated-message token profiles
Reported experiments used large locally hosted models and over 500 GPU-hour equivalents per experiment

Official repository README describes Python 3.13+ and dependencies including openai, pydantic, pyyaml, srsly, and tenacity; its README says Unlicense while LICENSE text says Unlicense and pyproject.toml declares MIT
Static inspection of public I-01_n2.json: agent 0 local maximum 827 equals expected global maximum 827, so this exact seed is locally solvable and ineligible for a communication-dependent ranking

sources.title: AgentWorld: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Collaboration of Multi-agent LLMs
facts_used: 100 human-annotated tasks and 100 augmented variants in a long-horizon multi-agent environment
Introduces Causal Collaboration Effectiveness using a graph of causal relations between actions
Evaluates large hosted/frontier and large local models; does not isolate matched message-representation effects

sources.title: Cost-Effective Communication: An Auction-based Method for Language Agent Interaction
facts_used: Dynamic auction allocates communication bandwidth using learned message-value bids and selects full, summary, keyword, or silence content levels
This is a learned interaction/content-selection policy baseline, not a fixed-semantic-payload codec comparison
